title: Curtailing Increase in Malay Drug Abuser Numbers
what_it_is: Curtailing Increase in Malay Drug Abuser Numbers

sections.label: Malay drug abusers statistics
sections.summary: The question asks about actions taken, whether Singapore is on the right path, and whether the problem's core is understood, noting arrests rose from 2,887 to 3,343.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Home Affairs (a) with recent statistics showing an increase in Malay drug abusers, what actions have been taken by the Ministry to curtail this trend; (b) whether Singapore is on the right path in combating drug addiction; and (c) whether the core of the problem has been understood to arrive at the right solutions and action.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: From 2010 to 2015, the total number of drug abusers arrested rose from 2,887 to 3,343.

sections.label: Methamphetamine laboratory seizure
sections.summary: More than 270 kilogrammes of methamphetamine were seized from the laboratory, 17 times greater than Singapore's total methamphetamine seized last year.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: More than 270 kilogrammes of methamphetamine were seized from the laboratory, which is 17 times greater than the total amount of methamphetamine seized in Singapore last year.

sections.label: Drug-free society efforts
sections.summary: Efforts to be a drug-free society must not let up, with continued prevention, enforcement and rehabilitation, and community and families keeping youths and ex-abusers from drugs.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: We must, therefore, not let up on our efforts to be a drug-free society.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: We will continue to improve our prevention, enforcement and rehabilitation efforts.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: The community and families have a critical role to keep our youths away from drugs and to keep ex-abusers from returning to drugs.

sections.label: Anti-drug learning and MUIS
sections.summary: Students had an interactive learning experience on drug dangers, and CNB is engaging MUIS to include anti-drug messages in youth programmes and adult courses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
sentences.text: This provided an interactive learning experience for students to learn about the dangers and consequences of abusing drugs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
sentences.text: This year, CNB is engaging the Islamic Religious Council of Singapore (MUIS) to include anti-drug messages into their youth programmes and adult courses.

sections.label: MENDAKI helping inmates
sections.summary: Over the past year, MENDAKI has helped more than 180 inmates.

sentences.speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
sentences.text: Over the past year, MENDAKI has helped more than 180 inmates.
